faqs.question: How do I optimize a headline for SEO and clicks?
faqs.answer: High-performing headlines should be between 6 and 12 words, include numbers or brackets, contain power words, and front-load target keywords.

faqs.question: What is the optimal length for an SEO title tag?
faqs.answer: The optimal title length is between 50 and 60 characters or 580 pixels on desktop. Use our SEO title checker and SERP preview to stay within limits.

faqs.question: Why does Google rewrite page title tags?
faqs.answer: Google rewrites title tags if they are truncated, keyword-stuffed, or poorly matched to the user search query.

faqs.question: What is a blog title checker and how is it different from an SEO title checker?
faqs.answer: A blog title checker scores your H1 headline for CTR (emotional words, numbers, length), while an SEO title checker validates your meta title tag for pixel limits and keyword placement. Our free headline checker does both — analyze your blog title and your meta title in one page.

faqs.question: Is this SEO headline checker free?

faqs.question: How do I check title SEO for a blog post?
faqs.answer: Paste your blog title in the headline analyzer, then use the meta title section to test title SEO with your focus keyword. The tool scores length, keyword position, power words and shows if Google will truncate your title.

faqs.question: Headline checker vs Moz headline tool — which should I use?
faqs.answer: Moz's headline tool is a solid classic for quick scoring, while our free headline checker adds a pixel-accurate SERP preview, meta title checks and unlimited use with no signup. Try both and keep the workflow you prefer.

faqs.question: What is the best analyzer for YouTube, book and Instagram titles?
faqs.answer: Use the same CTR rules — around 50–60 characters, one number and one emotional hook — then paste your YouTube, book or Instagram title here to check length, power words and truncation before you publish.

faqs.question: How long should a title tag be?
faqs.answer: Keep title tags 50–60 characters (about 580 pixels) with your keyword near the front. Paste yours above to see the exact pixel-accurate preview.

metaTips.titleTooLong: Title is too long (over 60 chars or 580px). It will get truncated.
metaTips.titleTooShort: Title is too short (under 40 chars). Add more descriptive keywords.
metaTips.descTooLong: Description is too long. Keep it under 160 characters.
metaTips.descTooShort: Description is too short. Describe your page in 110-160 characters.
metaTips.keywordMissing: Keyword not found in title. Try inserting it naturally.
metaTips.hasPowerWord: Title contains a CTR power word.
metaTips.missingPowerWord: Consider adding power words (e.g. "free", "best", "guide") to boost clicks.
